urn:csabs:axiom/Binary128-special-values.formalStatement: +0=−0 numerically, but sign bits differ; ±∞ ordered beyond finite values; NaN is unordered and NaN=NaN is false under IEEE numeric equality
urn:csabs:axiom/Binary128-special-values.name: special-values
urn:csabs:axiom/Binary128-special-values.statement: Zero, infinities and NaNs are distinct encodings with IEEE numeric comparisons.

urn:csabs:concept/Binary128.axiomBasis: IEEE binary interchange instance: bits=128, radix=2, precision=113, normal exponent range [-16382,16383], gradual underflow, signed zeros, infinities and NaNs. Rounding and flags are explicit environment parameters.
urn:csabs:concept/Binary128.basisScope: Defining interface and selected derived results for the operations listed in this entry. Not an enumeration of all consequences or all alternative foundations.
urn:csabs:concept/Binary128.definition: A 128-bit IEEE binary interchange format with 113 binary significand digits for normal numbers, signed zeros, subnormals, infinities, and NaNs. Rounding mode and arithmetic environment must be supplied separately.
urn:csabs:concept/Binary128.leanModelLimitations: No correctly-rounded arithmetic or exception/NaN payload specification has been proved; run and round are unconstrained client parameters. Not a complete IEEE model.
urn:csabs:concept/Binary128.mathematicalFormulation: The partial format instance has (width,radix,precision,e_min,e_max)=(128,2,113,−16382,16383), with subnormals enabled. Finite nonzero magnitudes are m·2^{e−112}, 0<m<2^{113}, −16382≤e≤16383, and m≥2^{112} unless e=−16382. This instantiates the unconstrained FloatingPointType interface, without an arithmetic-correctness claim.
urn:csabs:concept/Binary128.reviewStatus: editorial basis review; no machine-checked mathematical proof
urn:csabs:concept/Binary128.specializationNote: Instantiate FloatingPointType at this entry’s radix, precision and exponent range as specified by basisInstantiation; rounding and exception environment remain explicit parameters.
verificationObligation: Instantiate operations from FloatingPointType at this format; specify rounding, subnormal handling, and exceptions.
Use the stated carriers, equality, domain restrictions and semantic conventions; alternative conventions require an explicit variant.
